format.contentEdits: Generated content is changed only with built-in imagegen; accepted files use format conversion and lossy WebP encoding only.

assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: compact academic concept plate inside an original reinforcement-learning textbook website. Create a polished high-resolution landscape 3:2 image, ideally 1536 by 1024 pixels, with generous margins. Warm paper background #fffaf2, charcoal typography, restrained terracotta #b56746, pale taupe and muted slate. Flat two-dimensional scientific editorial illustration, crisp vector-like raster, fine consistent lines, simple meaningful icons; no decorative cover art.

Main heading, verbatim: "CHOOSING A LEARNING METHOD". Build a compact branching comparison, not a long flowchart. A small question near the upper centre says "Future effects?". One short branch marked "No" leads to a distinct left panel, "Immediate decisions", containing a simple target icon and the label "Prediction / bandits". A branch marked "Yes" leads to a clearly bounded larger region labelled "Sequential decisions", occupying the middle and right. Within that region present two alternatives side by side: a card "Fixed logs" with a stack-of-records icon and "BC / offline RL"; a card "Simulation" containing two small equally sized tiles: "Discrete actions" with "Tabular / DQN", and "Continuous actions" with "PPO / SAC / TD3". Use grouping and at most a few short connectors so alternatives cannot be mistaken for methods that all run together. Keep all labels readable, aligned, concise and correctly spelled. A calm shared footer reads "Support • Constraints • Independent evaluation".

The illustration is a conceptual method-selection guide. Do not draw a kiln, physical equipment wiring, quantitative curves, numeric axes, equations, tensor sizes, performance claims, safety guarantees, robots, people, logos, watermarks, or a tall multi-stage chain. Use the exact requested labels only.
assets.inspection: Viewed generated output. Future-effects branches and the fixed-log versus simulation grouping are correct. Discrete and continuous methods appear as alternatives, not a simultaneous pipeline. All English labels are readable and intact. No measured curves or safety claims.

assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: compact academic teaching plate for supervisory kiln setpoint research. Generate a polished high-resolution landscape 3:2 image, ideally 1536 by 1024 pixels. Opaque warm paper #fffaf2, charcoal type, restrained terracotta #b56746, pale taupe and muted slate. Flat scientific editorial illustration with consistent fine outlines and generous spacing; attractive, clear, no ornamental decoration.

Heading verbatim: "FIVE CHECKS BEFORE EXECUTION". Small top capsule: "Requested CV increment". The visual centre is EXACTLY FIVE numbered review cards in a compact 3+2 arrangement: three cards across the upper row and two centred below. Reading order is defined by large number badges 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, not a long connector chain. Card 1: title "Data", subtitle "Valid signals", simple clean sensor-record icon. Card 2: "State", subtitle "Current bounds", simple bounded window icon. Card 3: "Model", subtitle "Credibility / OOD", simple model-check icon. Card 4: "Rate", subtitle "Rate / curvature", simple smooth-change icon with NO axes or numerical values. Card 5: "Bounds", subtitle "Limits / permission", simple boundary-and-key icon. Make the exact order Data, State, Model, Rate, Bounds unmistakable. Do not draw arrows between the five cards; a subtle encompassing frame says "All five checks".

At the bottom, two equally clear outcome panels, not a winding chain. Terracotta-tinted panel: "Any fail" then "Hold setpoints & log", with small final label "Process continues". Muted slate panel: "All pass" then "Accept in simulation". A small footer says "Supervisory setpoint increments only". Sparse broad grouping is enough; the accompanying textbook supplies precise relationships. Never suggest that a check guarantees physical safety or that RL directly drives coal, air, or valves. No formulas, real measurements, performance numbers, dense wires, generic robots, photorealistic equipment, watermark or extra cards.
assets.inspection: Viewed generated output. Exactly five cards, numbered Data, State, Model, Rate, Bounds in a compact three-plus-two arrangement. Hold-and-log outcome explicitly keeps the process advancing; acceptance is simulation-only. Bounds and permission are kept distinct from the earlier rate check. No physical MV commands or claimed safety guarantee.

assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: original compact academic illustration for an offline reinforcement-learning tutorial. High-resolution landscape 3:2, ideally 1536 by 1024 pixels. Opaque warm paper #fffaf2, charcoal type, restrained terracotta #b56746, pale taupe, muted slate. Clean flat scientific editorial style, sharp vector-like shapes, consistent fine rules, comfortable white space, strong readable English labels.

Heading exactly: "LEARNING FROM FIXED LOGS". Use a balanced three-zone plate, not a long process chain. The upper zone is one shared data-foundation panel: a small stack of records labelled "Historical logs", a clock-and-eye symbol labelled "Time & availability", and three clearly SEPARATED archive compartments labelled "Train", "Validation", "Test". This is conceptual separation, with no numeric timeline, no data plots, and no labels implying future information is available.

The middle zone contains TWO alternative method cards side by side with equal prominence. Left: "Behavior cloning", a simple paired-action imitation icon, subtitle "Match logged actions". Right: "Conservative offline RL", a simple proposed-action token contained within a reference region, subtitle "Check data support". These are comparison alternatives, not successive stages. Use only two short downward connectors from the data-foundation group to these method cards.

The lower zone is one broad shared panel titled "Independent evaluation", with three simple tidy diagnostic tiles labelled "Return", "Costs", and "Uncertainty". Two short connectors from the method cards enter this shared evaluation group. A small footer reads "Fixed data • Separate evaluation". Avoid any return arrow from evaluation to the test archive and do not imply test-set training. No formulas, measured charts, numeric axes, performance claims, live plant exploration, safety guarantees, decorative robots, engineering wiring, logos or watermark.
assets.editPrompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Edit this existing offline-RL concept plate, keeping its 1536x1024 landscape layout, warm paper, terracotta/slate palette, typography, major panels and all existing correct labels. Make only these precise scientific-clarity corrections. REMOVE the two arrows from the upper Historical logs / Train / Validation / Test group to the two learning-method cards. In the now-clear narrow gap above the two method cards, add one centered, easily readable caption exactly "Fit on Train only". Do not draw a connector from Validation or Test to learning. Keep the two lower arrows from the method cards into Independent evaluation. In the bottom middle diagnostic tile, replace the coins icon with a simple boundary/violation warning symbol, and change "Costs" to exactly "Constraint costs", split over two lines if needed. Preserve "Return" and "Uncertainty". Do not add formulas, performance values, extra arrows, safety guarantees, or other text. This edit must make it unambiguous that the held-out Test archive does not train either method and that constraint costs are not monetary expenditure.
assets.inspection: Initial image had an ambiguous shared Train/Validation/Test group feeding learning and a monetary coins icon for costs. Targeted built-in imagegen edit removed both upper arrows, added Fit on Train only, and replaced the tile with Constraint costs and a violation warning icon. Final labels, split isolation, two alternative methods and separate evaluation are visually correct. No measured plots or guaranteed support claim.

assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: compact academic concept plate explaining short model rollouts in model-based reinforcement learning. Create a high-resolution 3:2 landscape composition, ideally 1536 by 1024 pixels, with generous outer margins. Warm opaque paper #fffaf2, charcoal typography, restrained terracotta #b56746, pale taupe and muted slate. Flat two-dimensional scientific illustration, crisp vector-like raster, simple meaningful icons and consistent fine outlines.

Heading verbatim: "SHORT MODEL ROLLOUTS". Compose a balanced triangular arrangement of three major regions, never a long horizontal chain. Upper-left region: a solid slate archive of records titled "Real experience", subtitle "Covered starting states". Upper-right larger region: a terracotta-tinted group titled "Model + policy", subtitle "Short imagined branches". Inside it show a few SHORT schematic branches of small outlined state tokens coming from one solid starting token; dashed connectors distinguish imagined transitions from recorded experience. No axes, no numerical steps, no exact tensors. Near the branch ends, clearly show two small diagnostic outcomes: "Credible" with a compact container labelled "Model buffer", and "Uncertain" with a stop symbol and "Stop branch". The uncertainty stop must terminate a branch, not continue toward the model buffer.

Bottom-centre region: "Policy update" with two visibly different input stacks labelled "Real" and "Model". One short connector goes from Real experience to the Model + policy group to indicate sampling a start. Another goes from Real experience toward the Real input below. A short connector from Model buffer goes to the Model input below. Do not add any other arrows; exact learning-loop relationships are in the companion text. Preserve clear separation between real data and imagined transitions. Small footer exactly: "Model rollouts are not new physical evidence".

No machinery commands, numerical performance curves, equations, measured axes, implied field deployment, guarantees, decorative people or robots, long chains, dense wiring, logos or watermark.
assets.inspection: Viewed original and final WebP. Real records are solid slate; imagined branches use dashed connectors. The uncertain branch terminates at a stop symbol and does not join the model buffer. The policy update retains distinct Real and Model inputs. Footer explicitly says model rollouts are not new physical evidence. Branch count is illustrative, not an exact rollout horizon.

assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: original compact academic concept plate about plantwide operational decision layers. Create a polished high-resolution landscape 3:2 image, ideally 1536x1024, with generous margins. Warm opaque paper #fffaf2, charcoal text, restrained terracotta #b56746, pale taupe and muted slate. Flat two-dimensional scientific editorial illustration, crisp simple shapes, consistent fine outlines and readable academic typography.

Heading exactly "LAYERS OF OPERATIONAL DECISION". Use FOUR generously spaced functional cards in a compact two-by-two grid, numbered in normal reading order. Top-left: "1 Goals", subtitle "Production & economics", with a production-plan sheet and restrained target icon. Top-right: "2 Supervision", two short labels "State & quality" and "CV setpoint proposals", with a simple observation record and target-window icon. Bottom-left: "3 Execution", labels "Gate & authorization" and "DCS / PID / APC", with an approval stamp and simple regulatory-controller symbol. Bottom-right: "4 Process", labels "Kiln response" and "Metric audit", with a tiny schematic rotary-kiln silhouette and measurement report. The kiln must be only a conceptual silhouette, no engineering instrumentation or fuel/valve wiring.

Emphasize the hierarchy through numbered regions and grouping, not a sprawling arrow graph. Include only these three short connectors: Goals to Supervision across the top gap; Supervision to Execution through the clear central gutter, with label "Setpoints"; Execution to Process across the bottom gap. A thin separate footer band has two clearly named feedback concepts with simple report icons: "State & quality feedback" and "Economic audit". Do not add return arrows. Exact feedback relationships are supplied in accompanying selectable text. Small footer caption "Supervisory proposals retain inner control".

No extra text, equations, numeric charts, exact sensor routes, tensor sizes, measured outcomes, robots, people, direct MV commands, safety guarantees, long chain, logos or watermark. This is a mechanism illustration, not a decorative cover.
assets.editPrompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Make one local correction to this existing 1536x1024 academic concept plate, preserving all four cards, all correct text, the outer three connectors, footer, color palette and composition. Inside the bottom-left "3 Execution" card, REMOVE the small Controller block, summing-circle, input/output arrows and feedback wire. Replace that entire small wiring-style icon with a simple flat rectangular control-panel icon containing three vertical sliders and NO connecting wires or arrowheads. Add the tiny icon label "Inner control" if needed. Keep the separate APPROVAL stamp and the "DCS / PID / APC" label. The icon should represent regulatory control conceptually, not claim a specific feedback topology or engineering wiring. Do not change anything else, do not add other return arrows or new text.
assets.inspection: Initial generated image added a miniature controller feedback-wiring icon. A targeted imagegen edit replaced it with a non-wiring slider-panel icon. Four numbered roles retain goals, supervisory CV proposals, gated inner control and process/audit. Only broad setpoint/role connectors remain; measurement and economic feedback are grouped separately. Kiln is an illustrative silhouette, not engineering layout. Labels are complete and legible.

assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: original compact academic comparison plate about causal reasoning in industrial operational metrics. High-resolution landscape 3:2, ideally 1536 by 1024 pixels. Warm opaque paper #fffaf2, charcoal type, restrained terracotta #b56746, pale taupe and muted slate. Flat scientific editorial illustration, crisp vector-like raster, thin consistent rules and generous space. This is a conceptual teaching figure, not an identified causal model or a measured chart.

Main title exactly "ASSOCIATION AND ACTION EFFECTS". Make TWO balanced panels side by side.
Left panel heading: "Observed association". At the top inside this panel is a grouped capsule "Shared context", with two small readable labels "Feed & load" and "History & judgment", plus a simple feed-record icon and history-clock icon. A sparse fork from this common-context group points separately to two lower cards: "Setpoint proposal" and "Later outcomes". Under Later outcomes write "Quality & energy". Do NOT draw a direct causal arrow between the two lower cards in the association panel. The point is that common causes can influence both actions and outcomes.
Right panel heading: "Effect to identify". Arrange three compact regions in a small triangular layout: "Setpoint change" at the top, "Process response" lower-left and "Later outcomes" lower-right, with subtitle "Quality & energy" beneath the outcomes. Two short arrows show Setpoint change to Process response, then Process response to Later outcomes; no shortcut arrow or reverse arrow. Include one small question capsule "Comparable conditions?" to make this a research question, not an established effect. Use conceptual setpoint-target, process-window and outcome-report icons, no real equipment wiring or direct MV commands.
A single footer reads exactly "Conceptual hypothesis — identification required". All wording must be concise, correctly spelled and legible. No formulas, numerical values, scatterplots, axes, apparent experimental results, claims that matching removes every confounder, photos, robots, decorative cover elements, logos or watermark.
assets.inspection: Viewed generated comparison. Shared feed/load and history/judgment context forks to both the setpoint proposal and later outcomes. The separate action-effect panel is explicitly a question to identify, with no shortcut or reverse arrow. Footer says Conceptual hypothesis — identification required. Tiny report/chart-like icons have no axes, numbers or measured meaning. No causal identification or beneficial effect is asserted.

assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: compact academic teaching plate about objective formulation and feasible decision selection. Generate a high-resolution landscape 3:2 image, ideally 1536x1024, with warm opaque paper #fffaf2, charcoal labels, restrained terracotta #b56746, pale taupe and muted slate. Polished flat two-dimensional scientific editorial design, crisp vector-like raster, consistent fine rules, generous padding, readable typography. No decorative cover art.

Heading exactly "FROM CANDIDATES TO A DECISION". Use FOUR numbered panels in a compact 2x2 grid, in normal reading order. Panel 1 top-left: "1 Account", subtitle "Units & time", with a simple candidate-record stack and unit-ledger icon. Panel 2 top-right: "2 Feasibility", subtitle "Check boundaries", showing two small candidate tokens, one tick and one cross; the crossed candidate has its own clearly separated small label "Reject / search". Panel 3 bottom-left: "3 Trade-offs", subtitle "Pareto & preference", with two non-quantitative option cards representing alternative feasible choices; do not draw axes, plotted fronts, data points or bar charts. Panel 4 bottom-right: "4 Execution review", subtitle "Independent checks", with a permission stamp and checklist icon. A maximum of THREE short broad connectors follows 1 to 2, the accepted option in 2 to 3 through the central gutter, and 3 to 4. The rejected token must not feed the Trade-offs panel.

At the bottom, outside the numbered panels, show two small contrasted concept labels side by side: "Preference budget" and "Search tolerance". These are separate concepts, not equal values. One clear footer says "Search tolerance does not relax execution limits". No other arrows, no Greek letters or equations, no specific thresholds, numeric objectives, performance claims, safety guarantees, real machinery wiring, tensor sizes, decorative people or robots, logos, or watermark. Exact constraints are explained outside the image.
assets.editPrompt: Make a precise correction to this existing academic illustration, preserving its 1536x1024 landscape composition, warm ivory paper, terracotta and muted slate palette, serif typography, four numbered cards, icons and all other wording. Change only these semantic details: (1) Replace the text 'Candidate A' with 'Feasible set' in the checked box in panel 2. (2) Replace 'Candidate B' with 'Rejected set' in the crossed box in panel 2. (3) The orange connector from the Feasible set must enter the TOP BORDER of the entire panel 3 Trade-offs, near its horizontal centre, ending immediately at that panel border; it must NOT extend into the panel body or point at Option X or Option Y. This represents the whole feasible set proceeding to comparison, not an already-selected option. Keep both Option X and Option Y equally unselected; retain their balanced cards. Keep the rejected set separate from the trade-off flow, next to Reject / search. Preserve the other two arrows between panels 1→2 and 3→4. Do not add any extra arrow, text, mathematical formula, chart, quantitative result or icon. Preserve all other labels exactly, including footer Search tolerance does not relax execution limits.
assets.inspection: Viewed the original PNG and final WebP using view_image. Initial artwork connected one accepted candidate directly to Option Y, which could imply a decision before comparison. A targeted imagegen edit changed Candidate A/B to Feasible set/Rejected set and connected the feasible set to the whole Trade-offs panel border. Neither Option X nor Option Y is selected. Rejected candidates remain outside the trade-off flow. The four cards distinguish units/time accounting, feasibility, Pareto/preferences and independent execution review; the footer explicitly states that search tolerance does not relax execution limits. All labels are legible; icons are conceptual and contain no formulas or measured data.
